stem: In 2022, a district in Rajasthan, India, had 300 solar-powered water pumps. A model predicts that the number of pumps will increase by \(6\%\) per year, so that \(t\) years after 2022 the number of pumps is \(N(t) = 300(1.06)^{t}\). According to the model, after how many whole years will the number of pumps first be at least 600?
solution: With a calculator, \((1.06)^{11} \approx 1.90\), which is less than 2, and \((1.06)^{12} \approx 2.01\), which is at least 2.
So the number first reaches at least 600 after 12 years.

explanation.A: Incorrect. This is \(100 \div 6\), which assumes 6% of the original 300 is added each year. The model multiplies by 1.06 each year, so growth is faster than that.
explanation.B: Correct. \((1.06)^{12} \approx 2.01\), so \(N(12) \approx 604\), while \(N(11) \approx 570\) is still below 600.
explanation.C: Incorrect. \((1.06)^{11} \approx 1.90\), so after 11 years there are about 570 pumps, which is still fewer than 600.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The 6 in the model is the percent increase per year, not the number of years needed to double.

verify:
t = next(n for n in range(1, 100) if 300*Rational('1.06')**n >= 600)
assert t == 12
assert value(choices[answer]) == 12
assert all(value(choices[k]) != 12 for k in choices if k != answer)
